title: Example 288's binding under its locales, through the permitted setters' effect contracts: kept on 6.1.14, refuted on 6.1.13 (the state stream's second consumer)
description: The state stream of the domain-advances brief, step 6: the second consumer of the permitted setters' effect contracts (example 286's proofs/beans/protected-setters.contract is the first, on 5.3.19). Example 288's proofs/beans/example288/adapter/ProtectedBinding#protectedKept binds one property value {field, value} onto a fresh ProtectedBean with id and admin disallowed by the patterns "id" and "ADMIN", the binder configured under LOCALES[configLocale] and binding under LOCALES[bindLocale] (root, en-US, tr-TR, az-AZ, lt-LT), and returns whether id is 0 and admin false. proofs/beans.py runs it on each release's four pinned JARs at bound 8, over ASCII simple names and any value, through the bean wrapper's stand-in (proofs/beans/org/springframework/beans/ProtectedBeanStandIn.java, sampled against the release's AbstractNestablePropertyAccessor.setPropertyValue(PropertyValue) before each run: 741,600 samples under the five locales, all equal on both releases) and the effect contracts of ProtectedBean#setName and #setTitle (proofs/beans/protected-setters.contract), which the run proves first and applies at the stand-in's setter calls, with example 286's models and observed initializers. Capped probes: 6.1.14 proved in 86 s (830 MB peak), resting on both contracts; 6.1.13 refuted at protectedKept(2, 2, "Id", "-9"), run on a JVM. Nothing of target.json or 288's adapter set changes.
expected: exit 0, two lines each '(expected X)' with the verdict X: bind-fixed verified (naming setName's effect contract), bind-vulnerable violation (run on a JVM)

resources.notes: each check took about 90 s in a capped probe, peak 830 MB (the simpleMatch lemma's proof is most of it); the stand-in's sampler prints about 230 MB, which the tool reads per sub-run

steps.name: example 288's binding at bound 8 on both releases
